primary_citation.popular_name: Management and control of community personal property; spousal fiduciary duty
primary_citation.location_in_code: Family Code, Division 4 (Rights and Obligations During Marriage), Part 4 (Management and Control of Marital Property), Chapter 2 (Community Property)
primary_citation.original_enactment: Predecessor Civ. Code § 5125 (enacted 1872); equal-management-and-control rule added by SB 364 (Stats. 1973, ch. 987), effective 1975-01-01; fiduciary-duty language added by Stats. 1986, ch. 1091 and Stats. 1991, ch. 1026; recodified to Fam. Code § 1100 by Stats. 1992, ch. 162 effective 1994-01-01.
primary_citation.amendment_history: 1975 (equal management); 1986 (fiduciary duty language); 1991 (full disclosure obligation; § 1101 remedy); 1992/1994 (recodification); multiple technical amendments since 1994.
primary_citation.positive_law_status: In force. Core substantive rules stable since 1994 recodification.

evolution_chain.description: Equal management and control rule enacted; husband's-management era ended
Fiduciary duty language added to former Civ. Code § 5125
Full disclosure obligation strengthened; § 1101 remedy structure added
Recodification from Civ. Code § 5125 to Fam. Code § 1100 with substantive rules preserved. Stable since 1994.

case_law.citation: In re Marriage of Lucas (1980) 27 Cal.3d 808
case_law.holding_summary: Joint-title presumption controls characterization; separate-property contributions do not create ownership interests absent written agreement (contributing spouse has reimbursement right only).

case_law.citation: In re Marriage of Rossin (2009) 172 Cal.App.4th 725
case_law.holding_summary: Spousal fiduciary duty is of the 'highest character'; affirmative disclosure required; duty continues continuously through separation until division.

case_law.citation: In re Marriage of Walker (2012) 203 Cal.App.4th 137
case_law.holding_summary: § 1101(h) 100%-of-value remedy applies to breaches that meet Civ. Code § 3294 fraud/oppression/malice definitions; § 1101(g) provides attorney's fee sanctions; duty continuous until division.

citizen_relevance.target_case: 2958 Honeysuckle house sale — community property acquired during Hartmann-Cerretani marriage; dissolution never finalized with proper property division; house sold with 19 unsigned documents and $496K unaccounted
citizen_relevance.doctrinal_theory: § 1100(e) breach of fiduciary duty + § 1101(h) 100%-of-value remedy + § 1101(g) attorney's fees + cross-reference to § 1572 tort fraud for third-party defendants + § 3294 punitive damages
critical_factual_inquiries: How was the Honeysuckle title held (joint, one name, trust, etc.)?
Was the marriage in force at the time of acquisition? At the time of sale?
Was the dissolution finalized with proper property division judgment?
What written consents, if any, were obtained for the sale?
Who directed the disposition of the $496K unaccounted proceeds?
citizen_relevance.sol_consideration: The § 1100(e) duty continues until division; breach SOL runs from discovery (Fam. Code § 1101 and case law); likely discovery-rule tolling applies to the Honeysuckle pattern
